subject: Streaming delivery: SSE vs WebSocket + initial TTFT & concurrency checklist
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Tay <sarah.tay@finpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-04-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Streaming delivery: SSE vs WebSocket + initial TTFT & concurrency checklist

Hi Sarah — great conversation this morning. Quick recap and a short checklist so we can size a pilot that validates the performance constraints you mentioned on the call. Please review and flag anything I missed.

Key context we captured on the call:
- App pattern: bank statement summarization embedded in customer portal (real end-users).
- Expected peak concurrent users: ~200 internal sessions hitting model-backed summarization flows during business peak (09:00–11:00 PT).
- Average request shape: 1 prompt + 2 short system messages, expected output ~250–400 tokens (mostly English).
- Throughput expectation: ~1.5–2.5 requests/sec sustained across the pool during peak; bursty spikes up to 8–10 rps for short windows.
- Primary requirement: keep Time-To-First-Token (TTFT) low for perceived interactivity; also support streaming so UI can render partial paragraphs as they arrive.

Initial performance targets we propose for the pilot (please confirm):
- TTFT (first byte) target: p95 < 120ms for interactive flows; p99 < 300ms.
- Streaming chunk cadence: app wants chunks delivered every ~100–300ms when model producing tokens (smoother UX) OR chunk sizes ~80–150 tokens if cadence is coarser.
- Transport: prefer SSE for simpler tabbed UI integration; WebSocket acceptable if you need bi-directional signals.
- Concurrency and scaling: pilot should validate 200 concurrent connections with 10% headroom (target test concurrency = 220).
- Fallbacks: automatic degraded path if streaming falls back to non-streaming (batched full response) within 200ms of degraded path detection.

Action items / asks from FinPay for an accurate pilot size and config:
1) Confirm TTFT p95/p99 targets above or provide alternate numbers.
2) Confirm preferred transport (SSE vs WebSocket). If SSE, confirm whether your front-end needs reconnection/heartbeat semantics.
3) Share a small set (5–10) of representative prompts/payloads and expected output lengths — we have attached a sample payload file and the MAP.
4) Expected SLA tolerance for occasional warm-up latency (how tolerant is the app to ~1s cold TTFT for first session after idle?).

Next steps (our side): we’ll provision a pilot environment (dedicated small pool) and run a combined synthetic + replay test to measure TTFT at p95/p99 and verify chunk cadence. I’ll include suggested load curves after you confirm the items above.

Thanks —
Aditya Rao
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
aditya@redwoodinference.com

From: Sarah Tay <sarah.tay@finpay.com>

Cc: platform@finpay.com
Date: 2027-04-11T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Streaming delivery: SSE vs WebSocket + initial TTFT & concurrency checklist

Thanks Aditya — this is exactly what we needed, very clear. Quick answers inline: 

- TTFT: p95 target of 150ms is acceptable; we can relax p99 to 400ms for the pilot. If you can demonstrate p95 120ms in later stages, even better.
- Transport: prefer SSE for simplicity (single-direction server->client). Yes, we need a heartbeat every 30s to detect stale connections behind our LB.
- Payloads: attaching 6 representative prompts (customer examples). Typical expected output lengths: 200–350 tokens.
- Cold tolerance: we can tolerate 800ms cold-start TTFT for the very first request after a 10+ minute idle period, but anything beyond 1s is a user experience risk.

Two other items:
1) Our security/compliance team will ask for a short note on connection TLS, client certs (if supported), and whether streaming connections are audited in the same audit log as rest calls. Please cc our security contact in the next message (platform@finpay.com).
2) Pricing: for the pilot we are expecting a credit-backed trial; we’ll loop procurement once pilot metrics look good.

Happy to sync tomorrow for 30 minutes to finalize load curves.

—Sarah
Senior PM, Platform
FinPay
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Streaming delivery: SSE vs WebSocket + initial TTFT & concurrency checklist

Perfect — thanks for the quick confirmations, Sarah. Couple of clarifications + proposed pilot plan below.

Clarifications:
- We will enable SSE with a 30s heartbeat. Connection audit events (open/close/errors) will be recorded and available in the pilot console. We’ll include a short security note for your compliance thread describing TLS ciphers and our transport auditing practice.
- Pilot account: we’ll stand up a small dedicated pool (2 x A100-equivalent instances with autoscale to +1 on sustained 80% utilization) and run a combined synthetic replay and live-run.

Pilot validation checklist (what we will measure):
1) TTFT at p50/p95/p99 under the expected concurrency curve (target p95 <= 150ms for pilot).
2) Streaming chunk cadence: measure inter-chunk latency distribution and percent of chunks < 200ms.
3) End-to-end UX: confirm UI reconstructs partial outputs with SSE heartbeats and handles reconnects within 500ms.
4) Failure modes: simulate one instance failure and verify automatic routing to remaining pool within 2s without request loss.

Proposed schedule:
- 2027-04-13: Exchange final payloads + security contact details (you provide), finalize load curve.
- 2027-04-15: Pilot provisioning and smoke test.
- 2027-04-16–18: Run multi-day pilot (synthetic + small % of live traffic).
- 2027-04-20: Review metrics and decide go/no-go for expansion.

Please confirm the schedule and drop platform@finpay.com into this thread if they have any extra constraints. We’ll attach the small security note and a short runbook for the pilot in the next email.

Thanks again — looking forward to getting this moving.

Aditya Rao
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
